title: Bearings
examples: How do I find the bearing if I already know the starting point?
What is the difference between a bearing and an angle?
If I travel north, what is my bearing?

explain.say: Today we will learn about bearings in geometry.
A bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north.
We measure this angle in degrees, from zero to three hundred ninety-nine.
If you walk north, your bearing is exactly zero degrees.
To find a bearing, you draw a line from the starting point to the ending point.

draw.text: Draw line from start to end

faq.q: What is the difference between a bearing and an angle?
faq.a: A bearing always uses north as its starting line. A general angle might start anywhere.
asks: What is the reference line for a bearing?
Do I always measure from north?

faq.q: How do I find the bearing if I know the coordinates?
faq.a: You can use trigonometry or draw a right-angled triangle to find the angle.
asks: Can I use Pythagoras for bearings?
What if I know the change in x and y?

faq.a: A back bearing is the bearing going back to the original starting point.
asks: How do I go back to where I started?
Is it just the opposite direction?

faq.q: If I travel east, what is my bearing?
faq.a: East is always ninety degrees when measured clockwise from north.
asks: What is the bearing for east?
Does east always equal ninety degrees?

faq.q: Do I need a compass for this?
faq.a: Yes, a compass helps you visualize the direction, but we use math to calculate it.

facts: The measurement always starts from the North line.
North is represented by zero degrees.
East is ninety degrees, and South is one hundred eighty degrees.
